rubric.basis: Original requests versus actual copyable B/C text; no reliance on self-declared drift checks or outside-block assumption notes. Review requested setup findings as context for the missing-prompt case.
rubric.counts: Atomic material findings. Optional strengthening is included in additions and separately counted. A stricter rule repeated as acceptance uses the same issue ID in additions/criteria. Category counts therefore overlap; distinct_issue_count deduplicates within each case.
rubric.not_drift: Harmless formatting, routine code discovery, ordinary evidence of the requested outcome, safety against injection, faithful decomposition and clearly optional suggestions.
rubric.clarity: CLEAR: directly understandable; MIXED: material ambiguity or misleading wording; UNCLEAR: unusable meaning.
rubric.readiness: READY: actionable with ordinary repository discovery; BLOCKED_INPUT: missing task/sheets/deciding policy properly left unresolved; UNSAFE_SCOPE_CHOICE: output selects or grants unstated scope.
rubric.provider_suitability: SUITABLE: interface-level text is compatible; MIXED: conflicting interface advice; UNESTABLISHED: agent unspecified. No rating proves model effectiveness.

limitations: One independent model reviewer, no human calibration or repeated sampling. Counts are review judgments, not deterministic semantic proof.
One final visible output per arm/case; synthetic public scenarios are not a sample of real production traffic.
A is the supplied request itself; zero introduced drift for A is definitional, not evidence of superior clarity or readiness.
Source pages were not live-refetched in this code review; knowledge provenance fields and applicability were inspected, not independently recertified.
Model/skill invocation claims come from committed metrics. Raw private traces and downstream results were outside this review range.
Prompt lengths are intentionally not quality scores. No production, real MR/merge/deploy or cross-provider execution proof is inferred.
